title: copies kept apart give back the name alias
line: John Y Davidson's death decided by the owner on FamilySearch's index entry, which names him as the tree does; the certificate's page, archived under the same citation, takes the decision as a copy, and its own words for him, John Young Davidson, become an accepted alias with it; the owner's word that the page is another record gives back what the decision carried to it, the alias with the link and the statements, undecided

steps.say: FamilySearch's index entry of his death, archived under the file's citation
the owner accepts the index entry as his: it names him as the tree does, so no alias
FamilySearch's page of the certificate, archived under the same citation: a copy of the record, decided with it

expect.why: the page's own words for him, carried with the decision

steps.say: the owner's word: the page is not this record

copies.note: harness: the page kept apart to see what the decision carried to it given back

expect.why: the alias the carry wrote goes back with the link and the statements: no decision on the page states those words now
